author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Choose ASTC texture quality in EmuCoreX
summary: Keep the original texture archive, compare one scene at different block sizes and check that conversion finishes successfully before evaluating the result.
heroAlt: Original illustration comparing 4×4, 6×6 and 8×8 ASTC block footprints

blocks.text: Use an EmuCoreX build with texture optimization and a device that supports ASTC. Keep the original PNG/DDS archive outside the installed pack folder. Close the game and leave free space for temporary conversion files. Conversion takes time and uses battery power. If ASTC is unavailable, keep the original texture format.

Open the texture manager and press Optimize pack on an installed pack. Choose the block size in the dialog before starting. Imports and downloads also offer a compression choice. Compare 6×6 first. Try 4×4 for fine detail, or 8×8 and larger for smaller files if you accept the quality loss.

Wait for conversion to finish successfully. Compare the same game scene at the same internal resolution. Inspect small text, faces, gradients and transparent edges. Record the block size and installed pack size. Larger ASTC blocks store fewer bits per pixel. Download size, installed size and runtime memory use are different measurements. None proves a frame-rate increase by itself.

Pause and Resume let you interrupt conversion. A paused operation is unfinished. Check the final status before launching the game. Some textures may retain their original format, so success does not mean that every file is ASTC. After an error, check free storage and access to the source archive before retrying.

To select another quality after conversion, import the original archive again. The converter does not repeatedly encode existing ASTC files. A smaller block cannot recover detail already lost. Changing a download default does not change installed packs. Keep the original archive until you are satisfied. To undo conversion, reinstall the original pack without compression and check the same scene again.
